Francis Ngannou is a Cameroonian-French professional mixed martial artist. He was born on September 5, 1986, in Batié, Cameroon. He is best known for competing in the Heavyweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), where he is the reigning UFC Heavyweight Champion. 

Ngannou grew up in poverty and had little formal education. As a child, he aspired to become a professional boxer, but he had to start working at the age of 12 due to his family's financial situation. He later emigrated to Paris, France, to pursue a career in boxing but ended up transitioning to mixed martial arts (MMA).

Ngannou joined the UFC in 2015. He is known for his impressive punching power and knockout ability, with most of his victories coming by way of knockout. He had his first title shot in 2018 but was defeated by then-champion Stipe Miocic. Ngannou won the UFC Heavyweight title from Miocic in a rematch on March 27, 2021.

Outside of MMA, Ngannou is an advocate for more sports training opportunities in Cameroon. He founded the Francis Ngannou Foundation, which operates a sports center in Batié. He is also known for his philanthropy work, mainly in his home country of Cameroon.

As of January 2022, according to the various professional analysis and sources, Ngannou is renowned as one of the hardest punchers in the history of combat sports, fashioning his nickname "The Predator". His knockout wins over notable UFC fighters have ratcheted up his fame to be one of MMA's most recognizable figures.
